scenarios.title: The One-Year Deal
scenarios.text: The offer is one year, the minimum, and a phone call that says take it or leave it.

choices.label: Sign it
choices.result: You sign it. A year is a year, and you still love the work.

choices.label: Test the market
choices.result: You test the market. Two clubs call, and one makes the same offer with more respect.

choices.label: Ask home
choices.result: You ask home. {love_interest} says, 'Do you still want it?' You do.

scenarios.title: The Veteran Minimum
scenarios.text: You're making a third of what you made five years ago, and the rookie next to you has your old car.

choices.label: Laugh about it
choices.result: You laugh about it with him. He offers to sell it back to you. You decline.

choices.label: Adjust the budget
choices.result: You adjust the budget. Nobody in the house misses the things you cut.

choices.label: Kick for the next deal
choices.result: You kick like the next deal depends on it. It does.

scenarios.title: The Body Says No
scenarios.text: Your hip takes an hour to warm up now, and Monday mornings take two.

choices.label: Build a new routine
choices.result: You build a new morning routine: heat, bands, a long walk. It takes ninety minutes and works.

choices.label: Push through
choices.result: You push through. Your hip complains all season, and holds.

choices.label: Rest more
choices.result: You rest more and practice less. You're fresher on game days and stiffer at practice.

scenarios.title: The Farewell Season
scenarios.text: Do you tell the world this is your last season, or let it end quietly?

choices.label: Tell the world
choices.result: You tell the world. Every stadium has a sign for you, and every week is a goodbye.

choices.label: Let it end quietly
choices.result: You let it end quietly. Only the people closest to you know, and that's how you want it.

choices.label: Tell the team only
choices.result: You tell the team only. The specialists make it their mission to send you out right.

scenarios.title: The General Manager's Office
scenarios.text: The general manager says they're going in a different direction at kicker next season.

choices.label: Prove them wrong
choices.result: You decide to prove them wrong, here or somewhere else. The fire is back.

choices.label: Ask your agent to look
choices.result: You ask your agent to look around quietly. There's interest, and it's modest.

choices.label: Tell your family
choices.result: You tell your family that night. Nobody panics, and that helps.

scenarios.title: The Comeback Workout
scenarios.text: Released last spring, signed this summer: everyone in camp thinks you're finished.

choices.label: Show them
choices.result: You show them on the first day of camp and every day after. By August, nobody calls you finished.

choices.label: Help the young players
choices.result: You help the young players from day one. You're the veteran they didn't know they needed.

choices.label: Prove it with numbers
choices.result: You chart every kick and leave the numbers on the coach's desk. They're good numbers.

scenarios.title: The Broadcast Booth
scenarios.text: A network offers you a job in the booth when you're done.

choices.label: Say yes for later
choices.result: You say yes, for later. It's nice to know there's a door.

choices.label: Ask {tyler}
choices.result: You ask {tyler} what the booth is really like. He tells you everything, including the early mornings.

choices.label: Say not yet
choices.result: You say not yet. They say they'll ask again.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Offer
scenarios.text: A college asks if you'd coach their kickers when you retire.

choices.label: Say yes
choices.result: You say yes, for when the time comes. You start keeping notes on how you teach.

choices.label: Ask for time
choices.result: You ask for time. They give it to you.

choices.label: Say no
choices.result: You say no. You want to be home when you're done.

choices.label: Tell them what you've learned teaching
choices.result: You tell them what you learned teaching younger kickers. They offer you the job on the spot.

scenarios.title: The Last Contract
scenarios.text: This contract is probably the last one, and your agent says so out loud.

choices.label: Make it count
choices.result: You make it count: every practice, every rep, every goodbye you don't say yet.

choices.label: Plan the end
choices.result: You plan the end with your agent and your family. It's calm and a little sad.

choices.label: Celebrate it
choices.result: You celebrate it with dinner at the place you went after your first contract.

scenarios.title: Your Kid Wants to Kick
scenarios.text: Your kid wants to kick in middle school, and asks you to teach them.

choices.label: Teach them
choices.result: You teach them in the backyard every evening. They're better than you were at that age.

choices.label: Let them have fun
choices.result: You let them have fun and keep the coaching to one tip a day.

choices.label: Find them a coach
choices.result: You find them a good coach, so you can just be the parent in the stands.

scenarios.title: The Ring of Honor
scenarios.text: The club wants to put your name in the stadium's ring of honor after you retire.

choices.label: Say yes with your family
choices.result: You say yes and call {parent} first. They don't say anything for a long time.

choices.label: Ask them to wait
choices.result: You ask them to wait until you've actually retired. They agree, and it gives you something to look forward to.

choices.label: Share it with the unit
choices.result: You ask them to put the long snapper and {holder} up with you. The club agrees to think about it.

scenarios.title: Cleaning Out the Locker
scenarios.text: The box from your old locker is still in the trunk. Nobody walked by while you packed it.

choices.label: Call someone from the old club
choices.result: You call {holder} from the old club. 'I should have come by,' they say. It helps.

choices.label: Unpack it at the new place
choices.result: You unpack the box at the new facility on the first day. New locker, same routine.

choices.label: Leave it in the trunk
choices.result: You leave it in the trunk for a few more weeks. Some things take time.

scenarios.title: What's Next
scenarios.text: Your agent, your partner and your accountant all ask the same question in the same week: what's next?

choices.label: Make a real plan
choices.result: You sit down and write a real plan: three options, three timelines, one budget.

choices.label: Ask your family what they want
choices.result: You ask your family what they want. Their answers change your list.

choices.label: Answer after the season
choices.result: You tell everyone you'll answer after the season. You mean it.

choices.label: Pull out the plan you already made
choices.result: You pull out the plan you started years ago. Most of it still fits, and the rest is easy to fix.
choices.lock_text: having prepared for life after football
